defects: Inequivalence hypothesis is wrong: uses `(v i : F → ℝ) ≠ (v j : F → ℝ)` (mere non-equality of the absolute value functions) instead of the gold's `¬(v i).IsEquiv (v j)` (negation of the proper equivalence relation on absolute values, i.e. v_i = v_j^t for some t>0); these are not equivalent conditions — two absolute values can be equivalent yet differ pointwise, so this hypothesis is strictly weaker/different from the gold's and changes the theorem's meaning

Topology setup is non-standard and likely ill-typed: introduces arbitrary `[inst : ∀ i, TopologicalSpace F]` instances plus a hypothesis `h_topology : ∀ i, TopologicalSpace.ofFun (v i)` where `TopologicalSpace.ofFun` does not appear to be a real Mathlib declaration returning a Prop (it looks like a hallucinated/misused identifier), so this hypothesis likely does not type-check or does not actually assert that the topology equals the one induced by the absolute value

Gold uses `algebraMap F ((i : ι) → WithAbs (v i))` (the standard Mathlib WithAbs type-synonym pattern to attach absolute-value topologies without diamonds); produced statement instead uses a bare pointwise-constant function `fun x i => x` into `ι → F` with an ad hoc topology instance, which is a materially different and non-canonical formalization of the diagonal embedding and its topology
Uses `Fintype ι` instead of the gold's `Finite ι`, a stronger/data-carrying typeclass assumption rather than the Prop-valued finiteness used in gold

hv_inequivalent is stated for all i j with i ≠ j (via an implication) rather than using `Pairwise`, and combined with the wrong condition above further diverges from gold's formalization of pairwise inequivalence
